items.title: RTX Video HDR for SDR films
items.detail: Turns SDR films and shows into HDR on an NVIDIA RTX card when your display is in HDR.

items.title: Smooth motion
items.detail: Matches frame timing to your screen's refreshes in Settings › Playback so 24 fps pans play cleanly without AI frame generation.

items.title: Updates from Exo only
items.detail: Exo Cinema asks Exo's update address for new versions and nothing else.

items.title: Smaller updates
items.detail: From here on an update downloads only the files that changed.

items.title: Your Jellyfin server is the library
items.detail: Home, Movies, Shows, search and History come from your server. Sign in once and it's all there.

items.title: What you kept is still here
items.detail: Titles Exo Cinema saved before this version stay in Watchlist and History. Press one to find it on your server.

items.title: No more freezes at Stop or Close
items.detail: A film whose host goes quiet is asked again, and never holds the window.

items.title: Your recovery code, shown in setup
items.detail: A new account's code now appears in the first run, where it was being skipped.

items.title: Settings in Exo's look
items.detail: A solid black sheet, cleaner forms, and the same sign-in everywhere.

items.title: Your look follows you
items.detail: Glass or Solid and Reduce motion, chosen on one PC, show on the others once you sign in.

items.title: One account sync
items.detail: Your watch history, settings and add-ons sync through your Exo account; the old mailbox sync is off.

items.title: Your account keeps Cinema in step
items.detail: Watch history, watchlist, settings and add-ons follow you to every PC you sign in on.

items.title: Set up with your account
items.detail: Setup asks for your account right after Welcome, and goes on offline if the service can't be reached.

items.title: Plays on PCs where it was refused
items.detail: Stream links open over IPv6 first, so a link your Jellyfin server hands out plays on every PC that has IPv6.

items.title: Plays when the server's links are refused
items.detail: With your stream add-on in Settings, Exo Cinema asks it from this PC when your Jellyfin server's links won't play here.

items.title: Plays from more Jellyfin servers
items.detail: A link the stream host made for your server's connection now plays through the server instead of being refused.

items.title: Faster search
items.detail: Search on a Jellyfin server answers in about a second instead of several.

items.title: Fresh stream links
items.detail: Playing a title again asks your add-ons for new links, so one tied to an earlier connection no longer blocks it.

items.title: A clean close
items.detail: Closing Exo Cinema no longer ends with an error behind the scenes.

items.title: No freeze for the anime upscaler
items.detail: Its first compile waits until nothing plays and pauses when a film starts, so a film never stalls for it.

items.title: The clock keeps time
items.detail: With the controls hidden, the time and the seek bar keep following the film.

items.title: Anime upscaler from the second start
items.detail: Once compiled, ArtCNN switches on at once for 1080p anime, with no wait.

items.title: Airing soon on Home
items.detail: Signed in to Jellyfin, a row after Next up lists the episodes your server has coming.

items.title: Another version when one won't open
items.detail: If the version Play chose won't open, Exo Cinema tries the next one, without a restart.

items.title: Jellyfin doesn't drop out on a slow answer
items.detail: A slow or dropped answer no longer marks your server offline; Settings says Not answering only when a second try fails too.

items.title: Crashes and freezes are reported
items.detail: On by default, with no address, title or file name in them. Diagnostics in Settings › About says what's sent.

items.title: No freeze at the first anime upscale
items.detail: The first upscale compile runs beside the window, which keeps answering while it works.

items.title: Jellyfin at every size
items.detail: The top bar and its buttons answer the first click at any window size, after Maximize and Restore too.

items.title: Exo Launcher's look
items.detail: The player's controls and Settings match Launcher's buttons, switches and rows.

items.title: Changelog in place of What's New
items.detail: The sheet shows each release's notes, so you can read what changed.

items.title: Smarter buffering
items.detail: Films load ahead, read-ahead follows your free memory and your connection, and Jellyfin picks the version your link can play.

items.title: HDR for films, by itself
items.detail: A film with an HDR picture turns HDR on for its screen and back off after, with no setting.

items.title: Your Jellyfin server
items.detail: Connect once with your server, name and password, and your library, progress and favorites are all there.

items.title: Exo Launcher's look
items.detail: New icons, Geist everywhere, and Settings' gear at the top right.

items.title: Files open straight away
items.detail: A file opened with Exo Cinema starts playing while the rest of the app comes up, and local files read only 10 s ahead.

items.title: Quiet while you watch
items.detail: Hidden player controls stop scheduling animation and video glass work.

items.title: Reliable player controls
items.detail: Typing and IME input keep their keys, and unusual track language tags no longer break the track menu.

items.title: Surround as it was mixed
items.detail: With an AV receiver or soundbar on HDMI, Dolby Atmos and DTS:X go to it untouched, height channels and all.

items.title: Made for your graphics card
items.detail: The picture is chosen for the card you have. A laptop with two chips uses its faster one while plugged in.

items.title: Seeking follows the video
items.detail: The seek bar and the time stay with the picture again, wherever you jump.

items.title: See where you'd jump
items.detail: Hover the seek bar for a picture of that moment. Drag as fast as you like: the bar, the time and the picture stay together.

items.title: Anime, sharper
items.detail: ArtCNN redraws anime with crisp lines and real texture, at up to 4K and back to your screen.

items.title: The best stream for you
items.detail: Best ranks a stream add-on's streams by their details for your PC and connection. Ask lists them all.

items.title: The right audio and subtitles
items.detail: The best recording in the language you'd expect, Japanese for anime, with full subtitles in yours when you need them.

items.title: Your poster in Windows
items.detail: Windows' media controls and Exo Launcher's mini player show what's playing with its poster.

items.title: Updates when you open it
items.detail: When a new version is out, Exo Cinema offers it as it opens, with one button. Nothing ever interrupts a film.

items.title: Your add-on link, when you need it
items.detail: Settings keeps a saved add-on link as dots until you click into it, and Copy copies it without showing it.

items.title: Reduce motion, your way
items.detail: Settings > Look has its own Reduce motion switch. It starts from Windows' setting, then only your choice counts.

items.title: Stays behind your game
items.detail: Exo Cinema no longer comes to the front by itself, when it opens a sheet or leaves full screen with another window in use.

items.title: RTX upscaling without the ripple
items.detail: RTX Video Super Resolution now upscales to exactly the size the video is shown at, so the picture no longer looks wavy or distorted.

items.title: Next to nothing in the background
items.detail: Idle or behind a game, Exo Cinema now uses almost no CPU, and much less memory while minimized. It uses half the CPU while playing, too.

items.title: Pins that stay
items.detail: Updates keep Exo Cinema pinned to Start and the taskbar. If 1.0.8 unpinned it, pin it once more and it stays.

items.title: Notices like Exo Launcher's
items.detail: Messages show at the top right, stack, and wait while you point at them. Motion and timings match Exo Launcher's.

items.title: Media keys and Windows' media controls
items.detail: Your keyboard's play, pause and next keys work even when Exo Cinema isn't in front, and Windows' media controls show what's playing, with its poster.

items.title: In Exo Launcher's Now Playing
items.detail: Exo Launcher can show and steer what Exo Cinema plays. When you close the player, the media keys go back to your music.

items.title: The newest .NET
items.detail: Exo Cinema runs on .NET 10.0.14, with Microsoft's latest fixes.

items.title: Your add-on link stays private
items.detail: Settings shows a saved add-on link as dots, so it never shows up in a screenshot or a stream.

items.title: A log that's safe to share
items.detail: app.log no longer keeps web addresses, keys, titles or your server's name, so you can attach it to a problem report as it is.

items.title: Newer mpv and FFmpeg
items.detail: The player is on the newest builds of mpv and FFmpeg.

items.title: The picture picks itself
items.detail: High quality on a dedicated graphics card, Balanced on integrated graphics or battery, and lighter for a video that starts dropping frames. Picture is gone from Settings.

items.title: Hardware decoding, always
items.detail: Video is decoded on your graphics card, and in software only when the card can't, so its switch is gone too.

items.title: AI upscaling on RTX cards
items.detail: A video smaller than your screen is sharpened by NVIDIA's RTX Video Super Resolution as it plays, when it's on in Exo Launcher's PC > Display.

items.title: Games come first
items.detail: While Exo Launcher has a game running, the upscaler steps aside so the game keeps its graphics card.

items.title: Updates that wait
items.detail: An update waits a few seconds for Exo Cinema's last helpers to close, instead of stopping at "folder in use".

items.title: The best version, every time
items.detail: When your server has a title in more than one version, Play picks the best one for this PC: one it can play as is, in the sharpest picture your graphics card is built for.

items.title: Or choose it yourself
items.detail: Settings > Playback > Source on Ask shows every version when you press Play, with its picture, size and sound, the best one marked.

items.title: Skip where you look
items.detail: Skip intro and Up Next sit at the right of the screen, larger and higher, clear of the controls.

items.title: Rows that page
items.detail: Arrows beside each row's name move it a page at a time, as in Exo Launcher's Store.

items.title: Pictures that lift
items.detail: Point at a poster or an episode and it rises a little toward you, as in Exo Launcher.

items.title: No white boxes
items.detail: Focus rings show only when you move with Tab, never after a click, and the search field has none.

items.title: Play starts playing
items.detail: A second click on Play no longer lands on the picture and pauses the video as it opens.

items.title: Search answers sooner
items.detail: Search asks your server only for what its list shows, so a large library answers in about a second instead of up to thirteen.

items.title: Search shows it is looking
items.detail: A spinner turns in the field while your server looks, and No matches or the reason shows when nothing comes back.

items.title: No ring on What's New
items.detail: What's New no longer opens with a white ring around Continue.

items.title: Your Jellyfin library
items.detail: Sign in to your server and everything you watch is here: Home, your libraries, shows by season, and search with Ctrl+K.

items.title: Progress that follows you
items.detail: Where you stop and what you've watched go back to Jellyfin as you watch, so every Jellyfin app picks up where you left off.

items.title: A native player
items.detail: mpv draws the picture with hardware decoding, HDR and Dolby Vision tone mapping, at the video's own frame rate.

items.title: Liquid Glass over the picture
items.detail: The controls blur the video under them as it plays, drawn on the graphics card at no cost to playback.

items.title: Audio, subtitles and speed
items.detail: One menu at the top right; each show remembers the languages you pick.

items.title: Skip intro and Up Next
items.detail: Skip openings and credits, and the next episode plays on its own unless you say not now.

items.title: A Home that opens at once
items.detail: Rows and pictures are kept on this PC, so Home draws before your server answers.
